question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Aunt Petunia was ______ a box of after-dinner mints.
solution:
The correct answer is "**passing around**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past continuous tense, indicating an ongoing action in the past.
 
• **"Passing around" is the correct form of the phrasal verb "pass around" in the present continuous tense, which is used to describe ongoing actions.**
 
• The -ing form of the verb "pass" is needed because it is being used as a gerund, which acts as a noun in the sentence.
 
 
• **Also, the correct adverb in the given sentence is "around" which means "in different places."**(आस-पास)
 
 
• Example: I know she is around somewhere here.
 
 
 
 
 
• Aunt Petunia was actively engaged in the action of passing around the mints.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, "passing round", is grammatically incorrect because it combines the present participle "passing" with the past tense "round".
 
• Option 2, "passed around", is in the past tense, which does not match the ongoing nature of the action described in the sentence.
 
• Option 4, "passed away", is a completely different phrasal verb that means "to die".(दम टूटना)
